about.title: Coalinga Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Coalinga is a small city, but its traffic isn't without risk — public records show 11 injury collisions and 15 people hurt in the most recent final crash year, with reports clustering on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. Corridors like Rt 33, Forest Avenue, E Polk Street, and E Elm Avenue see the bulk of reported crashes, often where local traffic, truck traffic passing through Fresno County, and daily commuters intersect. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the next steps matter: preserving photos, witness names, and vehicle damage before evidence disappears can shape how a claim is handled later. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect people who've been hurt with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of a Coalinga-area crash and explain options, without cost or obligation to move forward. Everything runs through a free introduction; there's no fee unless the attorney recovers something for you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Dealing with Insurance

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury suit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew or county vehicle — was involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline actually applies to your Coalinga crash.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage you're found responsible for, even if that's mostly the other driver's fault. How the story of the crash gets told to an insurer can directly affect that percentage.

items.title: Recorded Statements Rarely Help You
items.desc: The other driver's insurance company may call quickly and ask for a recorded statement — you're not required to give one, and an attorney can talk to them on your behalf so your words aren't used to minimize your claim later.

items.question: Do I need to talk to the other driver's insurance company right away?
items.answer: No — you're not obligated to give a recorded statement to the other side's insurer. It's often better to let an attorney handle those conversations so early statements aren't used against you. LawProactive can help connect you with someone before you respond to any adjuster.

items.question: What if my crash happened at one of Coalinga's busier intersections, like along Rt 33 or Forest Avenue?
items.answer: Corridors with higher reported crash counts, like Rt 33 and Forest Avenue, sometimes involve multiple witnesses, traffic camera footage, or nearby businesses with surveillance video. An attorney can help identify and request that evidence before it's deleted or overwritten. Acting quickly after a crash in these areas can make a real difference.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after the initial conversation.
